A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same u-µP work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–L support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original hyperparameter-transfer experiments, FP8 training at 1B–7B scale, downstream benchmark results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds controlled experiments on transfer failure modes, data repetition, warmup and learning-rate decay.

M1.justification: The u-µP components, embedding learning-rate rule, residual construction, independent search and FP8 procedure are retained. The corrected backward-scaling footnote in Table 2 agrees with the rule already present in v2 Appendix B; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText-2, WikiText-103 and SlimPajama, and retain the six downstream benchmarks in Table 4. The new SlimPajama transfer controls reuse existing language-modeling coverage; repetition and scheduling changes concern experimental procedures.

E2.justification: The µP, standard-parametrization and precision comparisons retain their comparator membership. New appendix experiments vary components and training settings; the newly cited model papers are not added evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 add substantial controlled evaluation designs: separate normalization and weight-decay interventions, intermediate training configurations, matched-token repetition controls, 500 versus 2000 warmup steps, and fixed or proportional learning-rate decay targets. Existing default and large-scale training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 8–9 disentangle the combined stability fixes and the transition from Tensor Programs V to Llama settings. Figures 10–12 test whether data repetition, warmup duration and decay targets confound transfer findings, substantially expanding robustness and mechanism analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs per point for Figures 1(b) and 5 and describe Figure 5 shading as 95% confidence intervals. No new seed-reporting, repeated-run-count or statistical-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Figures 8–12 add findings that non-parametric norms dominate transfer recovery in the tested setup, repetition controls preserve similar loss-basin shapes, and warmup or decay changes largely preserve width-transfer optima. These are substantial additional results under controlled settings. Existing headline curves and Table 4 benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: Table 2 corrects the output-layer backward scaling factor from 1/sqrt(fan-in) to 1/sqrt(fan-out), consistent with Appendix B. This is a local mathematical correction; Lemma F.1, its proof and the residual-scaling and cut-edge derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about simpler scaling, interpretable hyperparameters, efficient search, improved transfer and practical FP8 training. The added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 add substantive explanations of transfer failure and recovery and interpret the new controls as limiting repetition and scheduling confounds. Section 5.4 explicitly qualifies expected depth transfer. Appendix K newly explains why full-model efficiency is unmeasured and how software, optimizer states and sharding constrain expected speed and memory benefits.

D1.justification: New Table 6 documents the configurations underlying the existing Figure 2 comparison, including optimizer, architecture, initialization and training settings. The added controls also specify their interventions. Existing implementation guidance, hardware disclosures and code/checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Llama 2, OLMo, Qwen2 and two learning-rate-schedule studies, principally to contextualize decay choices in Appendix A.3.3. The main related-work discussion and positioning against µP and Unit Scaling remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds organized appendix subsections, locally rewrites Section 5.4 and expands Appendix K. It also repairs cross-references, including the unresolved reference in Appendix J. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 8–12 introduce multi-panel displays covering the new ablations and robustness controls, alongside the configuration comparison in Table 6. Figure 3 is redrawn with revised markers and a corrected embedding-rule legend. Most remaining appendix displays are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added controls strengthen confidence that the existing transfer findings are not artifacts of bundled interventions, repetition or scheduling, while Table 6 improves reproducibility. Appendix K makes the limits of efficiency evidence clearer. These are useful validation and transparency gains, although consistency issues remain: Section 4.1 still gives the old fan-in expression despite the Table 2 correction.
